title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): G is a graph decorated in the Mumford–Deligne way. It has vertices α ∈ S, a genus g_α at each vertex, and the set Î_α of half-edges and legs at each vertex. Grothendieck has shown that the fibred groupoid S ↦ M_G(S) of curves 'of type G' is 2-representable by a schematic multiplicity (a stack) iff each type (g_α, ν_α = card Î_α) is anabelian, i.e. 2g_α − 2 + ν_α > 0. That condition means G is stable, and for G connected it says G is an MD-graph (a stable graph). M_G is the corresponding modular multiplicity.

This page:
(23) M_G ≃ ∏_{α∈S} M_{g_α, Î_α}. Gluing curves along the edges identifies the moduli of curves with marked dual graph G with the product of the open moduli stacks of the vertex components, each with points labelled by its half-edges. In the margin Grothendieck corrects 'isomorphism' to 'rather, an equivalence', since these are stacks.

The group Γ = Aut G acts naturally on M_G. It also acts on the system (Î_α, g_α)_{α∈S}, by permuting vertices and relabelling half-edges, hence on the right side of (23). The equivalence (23) is Γ-equivariant.

(24) He then forms the 'multiplicité mixte' (M_G, Γ) =: M_[G]. In modern terms this is the quotient stack [M_G / Aut G]. A priori it depends only on the isomorphism class [G]. He interprets it as the modular schematic multiplicity, for groupoids fibred over the 2-category of schematic multiplicities, of relative MD-curves (stable curves) whose dual graph has type [G].

In modern language: the locally closed boundary stratum of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification M̄_{g,ν} indexed by a stable graph G is [∏_v M_{g(v),n(v)} / Aut G].

The next page notes that M_{g,J} ≅ M_{g,ν} for card J = ν, equivariantly for the symmetric groups. Since these are smooth of finite type over Z, so are M_G and M_[G].

Purpose: to set up the stratification 'at infinity' of M̄_{g,ν} by graph types. This prepares the study of the structure at infinity (Teichmüller tower, fundamental groupoids at infinity).
errors: (23) is first called an isomorphism; Grothendieck himself corrects this to an equivalence of stacks in the margin. The same imprecision recurs with 'isom. compatible aux op. de Γ'.

Implicit gap: identifying M_[G] = [M_G/Aut G] with the stack of curves of type [G] requires the gluing map to be compatible with Aut G and to identify automorphisms correctly. This is standard and true, but not argued on this page.
No genuine mathematical error is detected.

ideas.what: Moduli of curves with given (marked) stable dual graph G is equivalent to the product over vertices of open moduli stacks M_{g_α, Î_α}
ideas.modern_name: Boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} indexed by stable graphs; M_Γ = ∏_v M_{g(v),n(v)}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); graph-theoretic formalism systematized by Kontsevich, Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998), Graber–Pandharipande
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984): discussion of the stratification at infinity of M̄_{g,ν} with strata built from products of M_{g',ν'} modulo finite groups; given only in outline there

ideas.what: Quotient by Aut G gives the stratum stack M_[G] = (M_G, Γ), depending only on the isomorphism type of G
ideas.modern_name: Quotient stack [M_Γ/Aut Γ] ≅ locally closed stratum of M̄_{g,n} of curves with dual graph Γ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in the stable-graph formalism (Getzler–Kapranov 1998; Graber–Pandharipande 2003; Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions 'multiplicités modulaires' and strata; the explicit notation (M, Γ) for a 'multiplicité mixte' (stack quotient) is unsure

ideas.what: Terminology: 'multiplicité schématique' (stack), 'multiplicité mixte' (pair of a stack with a group action, i.e. quotient stack), 'MD-graphe' (stable graph)
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic stacks / quotient stacks; stable graphs
ideas.where_published: 'multiplicité modulaire' appears in Esquisse d'un programme

missed.claim: This is a historically interesting but mathematically standard explicit formulation by Grothendieck of the stable-graph stratification of M̄_{g,ν}, written as a Γ-equivariant product decomposition and its quotient stack. It predates the modular-operad formalism (Getzler–Kapranov) in which it later became standard. It is not new mathematics.
missed.quote: On peut considérer la multiplicité mixte (24) (M_G, Γ) = M_[G], qui a priori ne dépend que du type d'isomorphie [G] de G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's early, systematic use of stable graphs and quotient stacks for the boundary of M̄_{g,n}.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the now-standard description of the boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} as [∏ M_{g_v,n_v} / Aut G]. This was known from Deligne–Mumford and Knudsen and is outlined in the Esquisse. The only interest is historical: careful stack-theoretic phrasing and the 'MD-graph' terminology.
transcription_corrections: In (23) the left side should be M_G; the subscript is an overwritten G, not 'Ŝ' (the previous page ends 'on désignera donc par M_G la multiplicité modulaire correspondante').
The marginal note 'plutôt, une équivalence' is written vertically in the left margin next to (23). It corrects 'isom.'.
'courbes Mumford[?] relatives' is likely 'courbes M-D relatives' (Mumford–Deligne curves), consistent with section 4 on the next page.
'qui de sorte qu'on a' is likely 'de sorte qu'on a' or similar (the first line is cramped).
